clue.text: Incentive to hear this saint

indicators.note: to hear tells us to take the word for incentive as it is spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: a fillip is a boost or incentive

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to go and listen to a particular saint preach.
explanation.walkthrough: FILLIP (a stimulus) said aloud sounds just like the name of the apostle.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip was one of the twelve apostles and is venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Boy's on song, forming simple collections

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the boy's name above the song

parts.note: Herb is a boy's name; the 's is short for is
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A boy's singing is said to make up a simple compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple is an old name for a medicinal herb, so 'simple collections' are collections of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of dried plant specimens include medicinal herbs, once called simples.

clue.text: Religious type taking out some slut he randomly selected

indicators.note: taking out some says part of the following run of letters is extracted to form the answer

explanation.surface: A churchgoer picks a loose woman at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'slut he randomly'; 'selected' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teachings is a religious believer.

clue.text: Actor in theatre turned up late

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word for theatre is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rep is a repertory theatre
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: An actor in a play arrived at the theatre late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns REP into PER; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one who performs on stage.

clue.text: Untrustworthy as Janus

definitions.meaning: deceitful, saying one thing to one person and another to the next
the Roman god Janus is pictured with two faces looking opposite ways

explanation.definitionFit: A deceitful person shows a different face to each side, and Janus literally has two faces.

clue.text: "Deo Gratias" shows up in Yanks having it, possibly

definitions.text: "Deo Gratias" shows up in Yanks having it, possibly

indicators.note: in says the reversed abbreviation is placed within the rearranged letters
possibly says the letters of the words before it may be rearranged
shows up in a down clue means the abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: DG is the abbreviation for the Latin Dei gratia or Deo gratias, by or thanks to God

explanation.surface: Thanks be to God appears when Americans hold their annual feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows up' turns DG into GD, which goes into the anagram of YANKS HAVING IT signalled by 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American national holiday is a day of giving thanks to God, which Deo gratias expresses.

clue.text: Join stout friend in disastrous way

parts.note: stout means fat
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Joining a heavy companion ends in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join' only tells us to put the two words together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done with deadly or ruinous result is done disastrously.

clue.text: American's mood, going to a party in this state

parts.note: colour, in American spelling, can mean mood or tone
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An American cheers up by going to a party in this state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American's' signals the spelling without U; 'going to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the United States.

clue.text: Article in sort of old iron that's totally lifeless

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the rearranged letters
sort of says the letters of the words after it are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of scrap metal that has no life left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges OLD IRON into DOORNIL, and 'in' puts A inside it; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially dead as a doornail, the nail stands for something utterly without life.

clue.text: Such bench marks could be erratic I found

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the following words might be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the standards they were judged by seemed erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ERRATIC plus I; 'found' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Benchmarks are standards against which things are judged, which is what criteria are.

clue.text: Tragedy less hard to take in Verdi's version

indicators.note: less means the letter that follows is taken away from the play's name

parts.note: Othello is a tragedy by Shakespeare
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Verdi softens a hard-hitting tragedy for his operatic version.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdi's opera of Shakespeare's play drops the H from the title; 'to take in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera based on Shakespeare's play is titled in Italian without the H.

clue.text: Holmes had one — Dr. Watson, too?

definitions.text: Holmes had one — Dr. Watson, too?

parts.words: Holmes had one — Dr. Watson, too?
parts.note: Conan Doyle published a collected record of the detective's cases, and a medical man like Watson would keep a record of his patients

explanation.definitionFit: A detective's collection of cases and a doctor's register of patients are both named by the same word.

clue.text: At a cost of about a pound in old money

indicators.note: about says the price phrase goes around the pound letter

parts.note: for, as in sold for ten pounds
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from libra)
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something priced at around a pound, expressed in pre-decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLORIN was a British coin worth two shillings, a tenth of a pound, before decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a pre-decimal British coin, so it counts as old currency.

clue.text: Extremely bad light may

indicators.note: bad says the letters of the following words are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that the lighting could be very poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges LIGHTMAY; 'Extremely' looks like it qualifies 'bad' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally almighty is used as an intensifier meaning very great or very, as in an almighty row.

clue.text: International attempt to produce inflammatory strike?

parts.note: a test is a trial or attempt
a match is struck to produce a flame

explanation.surface: An international effort to provoke an incendiary strike.
explanation.walkthrough: In sport an 'international' is a match between national sides; cricket and rugby call it a test match.
explanation.definitionFit: A game between countries, especially in cricket, is an international fixture.

clue.text: Mother Nature's opening blast

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially livestock

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Mother Nature begins with a violent gust of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother Nature' reads as one figure, but it splits into DAM and the first letter of Nature; 'blast' is an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild curses uttered in annoyance.

clue.text: Duck initially and then trump? On your head be it

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: to ruff in card games is to play a trump

explanation.surface: A card player ducks, then trumps, and is told to take the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your head be it' is an idiom for taking responsibility, but read literally it describes flakes in the hair; 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurf is found on the scalp, so it literally is on your head.

clue.text: A hat with a rim specially designed for intriguing danseuse

indicators.note: specially designed says the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A brimmed hat is created for a seductive ballet dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'for' are links; 'intriguing' means spying, not fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: The exotic dancer was executed in 1917 as a German spy, so she intrigued.

clue.text: Work hard to produce painting on time

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the painting comes after the time letter

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: An artist must labour to finish a painting on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour is to work with great effort.

clue.text: Bear with primarily bloody obnoxious youth such as this?

definitions.text: Bear with primarily bloody obnoxious youth such as this?

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of each of the three words that follow it

explanation.surface: A loutish young man is described with a bear as his emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1950s Britain a TEDDY BOY was a youth in Edwardian-style drape jackets, often seen as a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s British youth subculture member was seen as an aggressive young lout.

clue.text: No such complaint when a kip-per's cured?

definitions.text: No such complaint when a kip-per's cured?

parts.words: No such complaint when a kip-per's cured?
parts.note: a kip-per is someone who kips or sleeps; once cured, they no longer suffer sleeplessness

explanation.walkthrough: 'kip-per' and 'cured' suggest smoked fish, but kip is slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Inability to sleep is the complaint that a good sleeper does not have.

clue.text: Deep split produced by clergyman and stupid person in church

indicators.note: in says the clergyman and fool are placed within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Rev is short for a reverend
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A rift caused when a vicar and a fool fall out in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier or ice sheet.

clue.text: Queen's entrance

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, and this is the little door she uses

explanation.walkthrough: A queen is the word for a female cat, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door lets a cat come into the house.

clue.text: Runs into loss, leading to poverty

indicators.note: into says the runs letter is put inside the word for loss

parts.note: a death is a loss, as in a death in the family
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A business making losses is heading towards bankruptcy.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity or lack is a kind of poverty, as in a poverty of ideas.

clue.text: Attempt to impress with style and taste

parts.note: to style someone is to name them
a drop is a small taste of a drink

explanation.surface: Someone tries to impress with elegance and refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually mentioning famous acquaintances is done to impress others.

clue.text: Lacking power, like Napoleon after seeing Elba?

definitions.meaning: the palindrome Able was I ere I saw Elba implies that after Elba he no longer was

explanation.walkthrough: The famous palindrome puts Napoleon's ability before his exile to Elba, so afterwards he was the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being incapable means lacking the power to do something.

clue.text: Lots of information, at short notice, returned to side

indicators.note: returned says the two preceding words are read backwards together

parts.note: an ad is a short form of advertisement, a notice
a bank is the side of a river

explanation.surface: A large amount of news is handed back to a team at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ATAD into DATA; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A store of information held on computer is a large collection of facts.

clue.text: Reasonable behaviour drawing mild praise from critic

definitions.meaning: a critic calling a drama a ... gives it lukewarm approval

explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and equitable conduct is called this, and a reviewer might describe a passable drama the same way.

clue.text: Gray's rhymes produced in the best period

parts.note: hey rhymes with the name Gray
day also rhymes with the name Gray

explanation.surface: The poet Thomas Gray wrote his finest verse in his prime.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray is the poet of the Elegy, but here the name only supplies a sound: two words that rhyme with it; 'produced in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's prime is the time of greatest success or vigour.
